To understand how buffer solutions work, let’s write the equilibrium expression for the ionization of a weak acid HA in the form

The concentration of hydronium ion depends on the ratio of the concentration of the weak acid to the concentration of its conjugate base. The key to effective buffer action is to keep these concentrations nearly equal and fairly large. Adding a small amount of base to an effective buffer takes away only a few percent of the HA mol­ e­cules by converting them into A2 ions and adds only a few percent to the amount of A2 originally pre­sent. The ratio [HA]>[A2] decreases, but only very slightly. Added acid consumes a small fraction of the base A2 to generate a bit more HA. The ratio [HA]>[A2] now increases, but again the change is only slight. Because the concentration of H3O1 is tied directly to this ratio, it changes only slightly.
